hypotheses.statement: The concurrency increase from 8 to 32 workers caused database connection pool exhaustion because the pool size remained at 20
The feature-flag service token expiry caused 401 invalid_token errors because the token renewal was not automated
The combined effect of pool exhaustion (38% failure) and token expiry (31% failure) produced the observed 61% failure rate, with overlap explaining why the sum exceeds 100%
The pool exhaustion began slightly before token expiry failures, suggesting the concurrency change triggered the incident sequence

observed_facts.statement: The database connection pool size was 20 and was not derived from the worker count
Pool exhaustion affected approximately 38% of settlement attempts
Token expiry affected approximately 31% of settlement attempts
The two failure modes overlapped on some attempts
Pool enlargement to 64 at 17:20Z eliminated pool_timeout errors
After pool enlargement, settlement failure ratio remained at 29%
Token replacement at 18:12Z eliminated 401 invalid_token errors
After token replacement, settlement failure ratio fell to 0.4%
The incident ticket INC-2201 recorded no settlement value at risk

open_questions.missing_evidence: Design documentation or configuration management records explaining the relationship between worker count and pool size
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from worker concurrency?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of service tokens with their issuance dates, expiry dates, and renewal automation status
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal and when do they expire?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Financial impact assessment or transaction volume data during the failure period
open_questions.question: What was the settlement value at risk during the incident?

summary: Payment settlement failures occurred due to two independent concurrent faults: database connection pool exhaustion from increased worker concurrency, and feature-flag service token expiry. The pool exhaustion began at 15:58:10Z, token failures began at 15:59:02Z, and together they caused 61% settlement failures. Pool enlargement at 17:20Z resolved pool exhaustion, reducing failures to 29%. Token replacement at 18:12Z resolved remaining failures, bringing failure rate to 0.4%.

timeline.statement: settlement-worker concurrency increased from 8 to 32 workers; database connection pool size remained at 20
database connection pool exhausted with pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising; pool_timeout errors affected approximately 38% of attempts
feature-flag service token expired; token was issued for 90 days on 2025-11-13 and renewal was not automated
calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token; affects approximately 31% of attempts, overlapping with pool_timeout failures
alert fired: settlement attempts failing reached 61% against objective of 2%
INC-2201 opened with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing'
connection pool raised to 64; pool_timeout errors stopped; settlement failure ratio fell from 61% to 29%
responder expected full recovery after pool fix but observed continued 29% failure rate
responder identified two independent faults: pool exhaustion from concurrency change and token expiry
replacement token for flags.internal installed; 401 responses stopped; settlement failure ratio fell from 29% to 0.4%
both faults fixed; questions remain about why pool size is not derived from worker concurrency and which other service tokens are on manual renewal
